examples: Many sailors perish at sea during violent storms.
بسیاری از دریانوردان در طوفان‌های شدید در دریا از بین می‌روند.
Without water, these desert plants would quickly perish.
بدون آب، این گیاهان کویری خیلی سریع از بین می‌رفتند.
The old manuscripts nearly perished in the fire that destroyed the library.
نسخه‌های خطی قدیمی تقریباً در آتشی که کتابخانه را نابود کرد از بین رفتند.
miniContext: To perish means to die or be destroyed completely, often in a sudden or violent way. Ancient civilizations sometimes perish because of war, disease, or environmental disaster. The phrase perish the thought is also used to say that an idea is so unpleasant one refuses to consider it.

examples: The hikers had to climb over jagged rocks near the summit.
کوهنوردان مجبور شدند از روی صخره‌های دندانه‌دار نزدیک قله عبور کنند.
She cut her hand on the jagged edge of the broken glass.
او دستش را روی لبه دندانه‌دار شیشه شکسته زخمی کرد.
The coastline here is jagged, with sharp cliffs dropping into the sea.
خط ساحلی اینجا دندانه‌دار است، با صخره‌های تیزی که به دریا می‌ریزند.
miniContext: Something jagged has a rough, uneven edge with sharp points, unlike a smooth surface. Mountain ranges often look jagged against the sky because of centuries of erosion and rock fracture. A piece of broken pottery can also be jagged enough to cut skin if handled carelessly.

examples: The rebels took him captive during a raid on the outpost.
شورشیان او را در جریان یک حمله به پایگاه، اسیر کردند.
The hostages were held captive in the basement for three days.
گروگان‌ها به مدت سه روز در زیرزمین اسیر نگه داشته شدند.
The captive animal paced back and forth inside its small cage.
حیوان اسیر داخل قفس کوچکش به این‌سو و آن‌سو قدم می‌زد.
miniContext: A captive is someone who has been captured and is held against their will, often by an enemy or captor. Throughout history, armies have taken captives during wars and sometimes exchanged them later. The word can also describe an animal kept in captivity, far from its natural habitat.

examples: The crafty fox tricked the farmer into opening the gate.
روباه حیله‌گر کشاورز را فریب داد تا دروازه را باز کند.
She came up with a crafty plan to avoid paying the extra fee.
او نقشه حیله‌گرانه‌ای برای فرار از پرداخت هزینه اضافی طراحی کرد.
The negotiator was crafty enough to get a better deal without anyone noticing.
مذاکره‌کننده آنقدر حیله‌گر بود که بدون اینکه کسی متوجه شود معامله بهتری گرفت.
miniContext: Someone who is crafty is clever in a sly or deceptive way, often getting what they want through tricks rather than honesty. In folk tales, a crafty character like a fox or a trickster usually outsmarts bigger, stronger animals. While cleverness can be admirable, being crafty often carries a slightly negative, untrustworthy tone.

examples: We decided to linger at the café and finish our coffee slowly.
تصمیم گرفتیم در کافه بمانیم و قهوه‌مان را آرام آرام تمام کنیم.
A faint smell of smoke still lingered in the room hours after the fire was put out.
بوی ضعیف دود ساعت‌ها بعد از خاموش شدن آتش هنوز در اتاق باقی مانده بود.
Guests should not linger too long after the party officially ends.
مهمانان نباید بعد از پایان رسمی مهمانی خیلی طولانی بمانند.
miniContext: To linger means to stay in a place, or to remain present, longer than is usual or necessary. A sad memory can linger in someone's mind for years after the event itself is over. Doctors sometimes warn patients that a persistent cough may linger for several weeks even after other symptoms disappear.

examples: The defiant teenager refused to follow the new curfew rules.
نوجوان سرکش از پیروی قوانین جدید ساعت منع‌رفت‌وآمد سر باز زد.
Despite the warning, the protesters remained defiant and stayed in the square.
با وجود هشدار، معترضان سرکش ماندند و در میدان باقی ماندند.
She gave the teacher a defiant look instead of apologizing.
او به‌جای عذرخواهی، نگاهی سرکشانه به معلم انداخت.
miniContext: Someone who is defiant openly refuses to obey rules or authority, often showing it through their attitude or actions. A defiant child might cross their arms and refuse to move when told to leave. In history, defiant leaders have sometimes inspired movements for change, while other times their defiance simply led to punishment.

examples: The rebels planned an ambush along the narrow mountain road.
شورشیان کمینی را در طول راه کوهستانی باریک برنامه‌ریزی کردند.
Soldiers were trained to ambush enemy patrols at night.
سربازان آموزش دیده بودند تا شبانه در کمین گشت‌های دشمن بنشینند.
The journalist felt like she had walked into an ambush of hostile questions at the press conference.
آن خبرنگار احساس کرد که در کنفرانس خبری وارد کمینی از سؤالات خصمانه شده است.
miniContext: An ambush is a surprise attack launched from a hidden position, often used in warfare or hunting. Guerrilla fighters frequently rely on an ambush to defeat a larger, better-equipped enemy. The word is also used figuratively, as when a politician is caught in an ambush of unexpected questions during an interview.

examples: The small bakery began to prosper after it started selling online.
آن نانوایی کوچک بعد از شروع فروش آنلاین شروع به رونق گرفتن کرد.
Farmers hope their crops will prosper if the rain continues this spring.
کشاورزان امیدوارند اگر باران در این بهار ادامه یابد، محصولاتشان رونق بگیرد.
A nation can only prosper when its people have access to good education.
یک ملت تنها زمانی می‌تواند موفق و شکوفا شود که مردمش به آموزش خوب دسترسی داشته باشند.
miniContext: To prosper means to grow, succeed, and become more wealthy or healthy over time. Many immigrants come to a new country hoping to prosper through hard work and opportunity. A business is more likely to prosper when it adapts quickly to changing customer needs.

examples: The butterfly will emerge from its cocoon after about two weeks.
پروانه بعد از حدود دو هفته از پیله‌اش بیرون می‌آید.
New evidence began to emerge months after the trial had ended.
شواهد جدید ماه‌ها بعد از پایان محاکمه شروع به پدیدار شدن کرد.
Several young leaders emerged from the protest movement.
چند رهبر جوان از دل جنبش اعتراضی پدیدار شدند.
miniContext: To emerge means to come out from a hidden or enclosed place and become visible. After a long illness, a patient may finally emerge feeling weak but relieved to be healthy again. In science, new theories often emerge only after years of careful observation and debate.

examples: The hungry wolves gathered to devour the carcass.
گرگ‌های گرسنه جمع شدند تا لاشه را با ولع بخورند.
He sat down and devoured an entire pizza by himself.
او نشست و یک پیتزای کامل را به‌تنهایی با ولع خورد.
She loves to devour mystery novels in a single weekend.
او عاشق این است که رمان‌های پلیسی را در یک آخر هفته با ولع بخواند.
miniContext: To devour something means to eat it quickly and eagerly, often because of great hunger. Wild animals like lions devour their prey soon after a successful hunt. The word can also describe reading or consuming something with great enthusiasm, as when a fan devours every new book in a favorite series.

examples: Despite his age, he still works with great vigor every morning.
با وجود سن بالایش، او هنوز هر روز صبح با نیروی زیادی کار می‌کند.
The team attacked the final match with renewed vigor after the break.
تیم بعد از استراحت با نشاط دوباره‌ای به مسابقه نهایی حمله کرد.
Fresh fruit and regular exercise can restore a person's vigor.
میوه تازه و ورزش منظم می‌تواند نیرو و نشاط فرد را بازگرداند.
miniContext: Vigor refers to physical strength and energetic enthusiasm for doing something. A young athlete often performs with natural vigor that older competitors must work harder to maintain. Leaders who speak with vigor can inspire a tired team to keep pushing toward a difficult goal.

examples: Please label the box as fragile before shipping the glass vases.
لطفاً قبل از ارسال گلدان‌های شیشه‌ای، روی جعبه بنویس شکننده.
Her health remained fragile for months after the surgery.
سلامتی او ماه‌ها بعد از جراحی همچنان شکننده و ناپایدار بود.
The ceasefire was fragile and collapsed within a week.
آتش‌بس شکننده بود و در عرض یک هفته فروپاشید.
miniContext: Something fragile breaks or is damaged easily and must be handled with great care. Antique furniture is often fragile, so movers wrap it carefully before transport. The word is also used for situations that could easily fall apart, such as a fragile peace agreement between two rival countries.
